solutions.check: 30 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

indicators.note: the words 'reveal' a run of letters sitting across their join

explanation.surface: A satirical glimpse of the Prime Minister choosing to let slip what the French President privately calls something.
explanation.walkthrough: The political names look like the subject, but they are only a string of letters to be read across the word break.
explanation.definitionFit: Merde is the French word for shit, so it is exactly what Macron would say.

indicators.note: the answer sits 'in' the following words

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a contract killer has gone to heaven, and answers that he certainly has.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark and the break before 'For' split the answer across two sentences; ignore the punctuation.
explanation.definitionFit: An enforcer is a heavy hired to intimidate or kill on someone's behalf.

clue.text: (& 13ac.) Repeating insertion of oxygen, gin, rum into port

indicators.note: the named letters are 'inserted' into another word
says which word receives them

blocks.note: the Kent Channel port, opened after its first letter
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A recipe of sorts: a sailor's drinks, gin and rum, poured into a harbour town, with some chemistry thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs on into 13 across. 'Rum' looks like a second spirit beside the gin, but it is the anagram instruction, and the gin is only letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An everyday idiom: to do a job over is to go through it again from the start.

clue.text: Weird forbearing type on crew – of use if you need a fix

definitions.text: of use if you need a fix

blocks.note: Job, the Old Testament figure proverbial for patience
to man a ship is to crew it; 'on' puts it after JOB

explanation.surface: An odd, long-suffering character joins a crew, handy to have around when something needs sorting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fix' reads as a drug habit in a Private Eye surface; here it is a household repair.
explanation.definitionFit: An odd-job man does small repairs, so he is useful when something needs fixing.

clue.text: Good swimmer, Phil Hammond's last piece on surgery

indicators.note: surgery cuts things up and puts them back differently

explanation.surface: Dr Phil Hammond, Private Eye's medical columnist, writes his latest piece about surgery, and happens to be a strong swimmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece on surgery' reads as the title of his column, but 'piece' belongs to 'Hammond's last' and 'surgery' is the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Dolphins are among the fastest and most agile swimmers in the sea.

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: An exasperated heckle: some wanker is interrupting the comic's act.
explanation.walkthrough: The rude compound 'jerk-off' has to be split: JERK is the fodder and 'off' tells you to rearrange it.
explanation.definitionFit: A joker is someone who makes people laugh, a comedian.

blocks.note: to sup is to drink, take a gulp

explanation.surface: A bit of schoolboy smut: someone's backside is being warmed, and they gasp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toast' looks like a verb about scorching a backside; it is the noun, a drinking salutation.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Bottoms up!' is said as a toast before drinking.

indicators.note: the word loses its top, its first letter

blocks.note: a protester is a MARCHER; drop the M

explanation.surface: A bare-breasted demonstrator turns out to be spinning a yarn.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeffrey Archer is a bestselling novelist and was jailed for perjury, so 'story-teller' is both his job and a dig at his lies.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeffrey Archer writes novels, and was convicted of lying under oath.

indicators.note: the word loses its last letter
the letters could be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: An official driving-licence handbook seems to have leaked government secrets.
explanation.walkthrough: The DVLC was the old name of the UK's driving licence agency. 10/24ac is the Official Secrets Act, which you break by revealing classified information.
explanation.definitionFit: Divulging classified information is exactly how the Official Secrets Act is broken.

clue.text: (& 24ac.) Self-sacrifice and TACO – about time for legislation to stop public information leaks

definitions.text: legislation to stop public information leaks

indicators.note: the letters are moved about

explanation.surface: A political jibe: TACO, the 'Trump Always Chickens Out' taunt, set beside self-sacrifice, with a call for a law against leaks.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs on into 24 across. TACO really is an acronym, 'Trump Always Chickens Out', which gives the surface its bite; for the wordplay only its letters matter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Official Secrets Act is the UK law that criminalises leaking classified government information.

blocks.note: sch. is the abbreviation for school

explanation.surface: A complaint that the equipment at a school is shoddy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trashy' looks like a description of worn-out gear; it is the definition, meaning tasteless.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitsch is garish, tasteless art or decoration, which is trashy.

blocks.note: the surface reads it as an insult; the setter means slang for drugs, cannabis especially
not a market-stall holder but someone who deals on street corners

explanation.surface: A sneer at a hopeless market-stall seller.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'shit' as an insult and you picture a bad costermonger; read it as slang for cannabis and he is selling it.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug pusher sells illegal drugs, often called shit, on the street.

indicators.note: the letters are moved about

explanation.surface: Someone moans about the life of a lumberjack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whinge' means moan in British English. The question mark flags that hewing is only one thing a lumberjack does.
explanation.definitionFit: Hewing means chopping wood, which is what being a lumberjack involves.

clue.text: An actual hospital bed occupant? Smart, cool!

explanation.surface: Someone lying in a hospital bed gets told they look smart and cool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Actual' separates an inpatient, who really occupies a bed overnight, from an outpatient who just visits.
explanation.definitionFit: An inpatient is admitted to hospital and occupies a bed there.

indicators.note: the answer sits 'in' the next word

explanation.surface: A translation note: this is the word for 'handles' in Vietnamese.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make 'Handles' look like a word being translated; it is the definition, slang for names.
explanation.definitionFit: A handle is slang for a name or nickname.

clue.text: After continental drink, gives up car

indicators.note: the next piece comes after the first

blocks.note: the drink is the sea, and mer is French for sea

explanation.surface: Someone who has had a drink abroad sensibly surrenders the car keys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The drink' is slang for the sea, and 'continental' asks for the French word.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Mercedes-Benz is one make of car, the German luxury brand.

clue.text: Saffron's source of employment in footwear

definitions.note: the definition is singular; the answer is plural, since saffron comes from many crocuses

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

explanation.surface: A spice merchant finds work in the shoe trade.
explanation.walkthrough: Crocs are a brand of chunky foam clog. The possessive 'Saffron's' dresses the spice up as a person looking for work.
explanation.definitionFit: Saffron is the dried stigmas of a crocus, so crocuses are its source.

clue.text: Hull: first class return in stages

indicators.note: a return journey goes back the way it came

blocks.note: the pod is the hull of a pea or bean
A1 = first class, with the 1 read as I

explanation.surface: A travel note: in the Yorkshire port of Hull, a first-class return ticket is bought in stages.
explanation.walkthrough: Hull looks like the city, and 'return' like a train ticket; it is a seed case, and AI is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Podia is the plural of podium, a raised platform or stage.

clue.text: Eye's impounded by government agency – flipping harsh!

indicators.note: one piece is shut up inside another
the whole assembly is flipped over

blocks.note: private eyes are detectives, 'tecs; CIA holds them after CI

explanation.surface: An outraged Private Eye protests that the CIA has seized its copies, calling it outrageously harsh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eye's' is read as 'eyes', private eyes, not the magazine; CI-TECS-A is then read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascetic means severely self-denying, austere, and so harsh.

clue.text: Bang in the middle of miniature portrait

indicators.note: the answer lies inside the following words

explanation.surface: Something sits bang in the centre of a small painted portrait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bang in the middle' reads as one phrase meaning exactly central; 'Bang' is the definition and the rest is the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A report is the loud noise of a gun going off, a bang.

explanation.surface: A pub scene: someone of middling size is told to get lost when asking about the next round of drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clear off!' reads as a brusque dismissal, but CLEAR is the fodder and 'off' the instruction. 'Medium' is a psychic.
explanation.definitionFit: An oracle, like a medium, passes on messages from the spirit world.

indicators.note: backing means moving in reverse, as a car backs, so the word is read from its end

blocks.note: tarp, short for tarpaulin, a waterproof sheet

explanation.surface: A crude joke about what an idiot uses to protect his bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' looks like the lining of a sheet, but it means TARP is read in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Wanker and prat are both British insults for a contemptible fool.

indicators.note: the answer is carried inside the following words

explanation.surface: A diplomatic move made by the American envoy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steps' reads as political measures; it is the dance steps of the samba.
explanation.definitionFit: The samba is a Brazilian dance, a set of steps.

explanation.surface: Something foul turns up for the second time in succession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a row' reads as consecutively; 'a row' is the definition, a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in informal British English: a scrap is a brawl or squabble, as a row is.

clue.text: Cry "Get lost!" when bored by economics head

indicators.note: the word has another piece bored into it
the head of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: the first letter of Economics; it goes after SCR

explanation.surface: A student yells at a dull economics lecturer to go away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bored by' suggests tedium in the lecture hall; here it means drilled into.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a scream is a shrill cry, of fear or of fury like the one in the surface.

clue.text: Herpes outbreak covered by rejected Sunday Times hacks

indicators.note: the anagram goes inside the next piece
that piece is turned back

blocks.note: ST is the usual short form of the Sunday Times; turned round, T and S wrap the rest

explanation.surface: A tabloid scandal: an outbreak of herpes hushed up by Sunday Times journalists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hacks' is Private Eye's word for journalists, so the surface already describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hacks is a dismissive word for journalists, collectively the press.

clue.text: Trial marriage: it needs a lot of balls

definitions.text: it needs a lot of balls

explanation.surface: A trial marriage takes plenty of nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: A test match is a multi-day international cricket match, in which hundreds of balls are bowled; 'balls' as courage is the decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: A test match lasts up to five days, so a great many balls are bowled.

blocks.note: Bath is a spa town in Somerset, and a spa bath is one too

explanation.surface: A seedy evening for a creep: a soak in the tub, then some bondage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jerk' looks like an insult for the man in the surface; it is the definition, an involuntary twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A spasm is a sudden involuntary jerk of a muscle.
